description_full: Donnelley Financial Solutions, Inc. provides compliance and regulatory software and services in the United States, Asia, Europe, Canada, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Capital Markets  Software Solutions (CM-SS); Capital Markets  Compliance and Communications Management (CM-CCM); Investment Companies  Software Solutions (IC-SS); and Investment Companies  Compliance and Communications Management (IC-CCM). The CM-SS segment provides Venue and ActiveDisclosure solutions to public and private companies to manage public and private transactional and compliance processes; collaborate; and tag, validate, and file SEC documents. The CM-CCM segment offers tech-enabled services and print and distribution solutions to public and private companies for deal solutions and SEC compliance requirements. The IC-SS segment provides clients with the Arc Suite platform that contains a comprehensive suite of cloud-based solutions, including ArcDigital, ArcReporting, ArcPro, and ArcRegulatory, as well as services that enable storage and management of compliance and regulatory information in a self-service and central repository for accessing, assembling, editing, translating, rendering, and submitting documents to regulators and investors. The IC-CCM segment offers tech-enabled solutions for creating, filing and distributing regulatory communications, and solutions for investor communications, as well as iXBRL-formatted filings pursuant for Investment Company Act through the SEC's EDGAR system. This segment provides turnkey proxy services, including discovery, planning and implementation, print and mail management, solicitation, tabulation services, stockholder meeting review, and expert support. The company was founded in 1983 and is headquartered in Lancaster, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Donnelley Financial Solutions,  is a small-cap technology business with a $1.7B market cap on $767M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 21% against a 10% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $108M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 5.09× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.9×.
Management returns a meaningful 11.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 5.1% of the shares.

The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 66%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $62.06 to $121 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 5pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.7x net debt to EBITDA ($24.5M of cash against $171.3M of debt), with interest covered 10.9x.
Goodwill makes up 51% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -2.7% over 3 years and -3.0% over 5 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 1% of profits supports about 0.2% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -2.6% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 7.4% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 7, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 5.1%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 95%.
Insider trading is two-way: 3 purchases and 17 sales over the past year, net $10.3M sold.
It returns 11.0% a year to shareholders (11.0% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 5.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 1,750 employees, each generates about $438K of revenue, 1.2x the Technology median, and revenue has fallen 2.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $62K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.1M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (3/10, lower is better).
